articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 11 published per cycle (58 vs 57 yesterday); 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one. Nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Science fell to 3 from 5, against a goal of 5 per day; all three came from science outlets (Carbon Brief, Phys.org, New Scientist), and two were climate measurements (Greenland ice, WMO greenhouse gases). Multi-source held at 28% (16 of 58) for a second day, just under the 30% target, with tech again leaning on single outlets (16 tech stories, mostly from one source each).
watching: Brazil after the runoff: Bolsonaro reported fleeing to the US, firms moving out of the real, and US lawmakers pressing Meta over Brazil.
Iran: Khamenei backing peace conditions, Saudi-Iran talks in Tehran, and Iran threatening Sinokor tankers.
Jordanian strikes in southern Syria and reports of UAE aid to Ansarallah in Yemen.
Russia-Ukraine: an Oleshky local truce, Lavrov predicting escalation, and Nordic leaders calling Putin.
Cyclone Arnab nearing India's Odisha coast at Ganjam.
Egypt closing Mada Masr, which is one of the pipeline's own sources and may stop publishing.
coverageGaps: Eleven datelines are a country or region rather than a city (United States ×7, China ×3, Europe ×1), against twelve yesterday; the missing-dateline metric does not catch them.
No Oceania story today, and Africa had five (Nigeria ×3, Cameroon, Mozambique).
Science reached 3 against a goal of 5; under the 2026-09-26 decision the floor may go unmet, so the remedy is wider science sources, not a higher floor.
Multi-source stuck at 28% for two days; most tech and crypto stories (CoinDesk ×4, Ars Technica ×4) rest on one outlet.
context: Output held at 58 across five completed cycles, with freshness at a 0.1-day median and no duplicates, quarantines or state-only stories. Latin America rose to 14% of datelines (Brazil, Guatemala, Honduras, Venezuela), and no source exceeded 10%. The experiment pause holds until 2026-11-05 for the runner cut-over, so the science shortfall and the multi-source dip are recorded for the next round rather than acted on.
